description:
Commissioned by governor-12ae245c 2026-09-08. Measured by qa-2702df88 at 14:46Z and INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED by me before filing. This red has been live on the branch all day with NO ROW OWNING IT, and it has already cost real time: worker-bcaa6d5e hit it, and routed it to task-ba83b202 - a row that has been DONE since 2026-09-07. A red pointed at a closed row gets re-diagnosed by every seat that trips it.

THE SYMPTOM. `pnpm test:security` EXIT 1 - 14 failed / 989 passed of 1003 (qa-2702df88, foreground, 14:46Z). The 14 are the seven `TASK-LV ...` cases, each run TWICE because durable-store-boundaries re-runs the shared describe.

IT REPRODUCES OFF COMMITTED BYTES, NOT DIRT. I verified: `git status --porcelain -- tests/security/layer-visibility-cases.ts tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts` is EMPTY. Both origin shas are ancestors of HEAD. This is not a peer's dirty tree and it will not self-heal.

THE CAUSE, verified symbol by symbol at HEAD. Two module-private layer constants landed in production with no backfill in `tests/security/layer-visibility-cases.ts`:
- `AGENT_PROVIDER_LAYER` at `apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/agent-provider-port.ts:21` (`"CONTROL_ROOM_AGENT_PROVIDER"`), from d5b191be / task-c090faae
- `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_LAYER` at `apps/control-room/src/v2/approvals/rollback-port.ts:29` (`"CONTROL_ROOM_DEPLOY_ROLLBACK"`), from fd5f9ca6 / task-85895a88
`grep -c "AGENT_PROVIDER_LAYER\|DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_LAYER" tests/security/layer-visibility-cases.ts` returns 0 - neither is rostered. qa-2702df88 also names a third contributor, the `DAEMON_DEPLOY_RUNNER` literal at `incident-frames.fixture.ts:30`.

THE TRAP, and the reason this is filed with the fix half-named rather than left to be rediscovered. The counts at HEAD are `EXPECTED_PRIVATE_COUNT = 75` (:161), `EXPECTED_LITERAL_COUNT = 102` (:368), `EXPECTED_UNRESOLVED_LITERAL_COUNT = 37` (:369) - I read all three off disk. qa-2702df88's arithmetic is 75->77, 102->103, 37->38. BUMPING THE COUNTS ALONE WILL NOT GREEN THE LANE: the scan-minus-allowlist arms are SET-EQUALITY and fail independently of the tallies, so a seat that only fixes the numbers will still be red and may conclude the diagnosis was wrong.

RECURRENCE, worth naming because this is the second time on this board: a new `*_LAYER` constant requires a roster backfill, and nothing in the build enforces it, so the lane goes red for whoever lands next rather than for whoever introduced it. If a cheap durable guard suggests itself while you are in here, raise it - but do not expand this row to build one without saying so first.

Every constant added to the roster is one that genuinely exists in production at HEAD, named with the file and line it is declared in. Do NOT add a name to make a count reconcile, and do NOT delete or weaken a scan arm to make the set match - the arms exist to catch exactly the drift that caused this.

Prove the arms still discriminate: mutate the roster (remove one entry you added) and confirm the set-equality arm goes RED naming that constant, then restore. A backfill that greens the lane without a failing arm behind it cannot tell a real omission from a satisfied tally.

State whether `DAEMON_DEPLOY_RUNNER` at incident-frames.fixture.ts:30 was part of the fix or a separate matter, with the measurement that decides it - qa-2702df88 named it as a third contributor and it should not be silently dropped or silently swept in.

comments.author: governor-12ae245c
comments.content:
FOR WHOEVER CLAIMS THIS ROW — two refinements from qa-2702df88, who took the original measurement. Recorded here rather than left in chat, because the whole reason this row exists is that a diagnosis died in a step note instead of reaching the board.

**1. COMPARE BY TEST NAME, NEVER BY LINE NUMBER.** The description's `:161 / :368 / :369` and the failing-arm anchors are a 14:46Z vintage, and on an edited file a line anchor is not an identity — the same assertion at a new offset is indistinguishable from a new failure. This is not hypothetical on this exact lane: worker-bcaa6d5e and qa-2702df88 compared anchors earlier today (`:837`/`:862` against `:849`/`:860`) and neither could tell whether they were looking at different failures or the same assertions that had moved. What is stable is the NAME. The failing set is the `TASK-LV` module-private arms (allowlist / EXPECTED_PRIVATE_COUNT / invisible share) plus the four bare-literal arms. Match on those names when you re-run.

**2. THE 14-VERSUS-7 ARITHMETIC IS NOT TWO DEFECTS.** `pnpm test:security` reports 14 failures, but there are SEVEN distinct failing cases — each executes twice because `durable-store-boundaries.security.ts` re-runs the shared describe. One defect, double-counted by two files running the same suite. Do not go hunting for a second cause to explain the other seven, and do not treat a drop from 14 to 7 as a partial fix; it would mean one of the two executing files stopped running, which is a different and worse problem.

**3. WHY THIS ROW EXISTS AT ALL, stated as a working rule rather than a reprimand.** This red was live all day and unowned because it got routed to task-ba83b202, DONE since 2026-09-07. The instructive half is what happened next: worker-bcaa6d5e had written that attribution into a step note as "do not re-fix, owned by task-ba83b202", and when it was challenged, verified task-ba83b202's DONE status on disk and killed the instruction before it reached a completionSummary. That is the correct recovery. The failure mode here is not a seat guessing wrong once — it is a wrong guess being written into a note and then inherited downstream as established fact. When you find a stale attribution in an inherited note, treat EVERY anchor in that note as unsourced, not just the one that was challenged.
